notes: The breadboard in the image is drawn with rows f-j in the upper half and a-e in the lower half, so I used the row letters to pick the bank: f-j is bank 'b' and a-e is bank 't'.

The pushbutton straddles the centre gap, with legs in columns 4 and 6. The catalogue says 1.l and 1.r are always joined, and 2.l and 2.r likewise. I treated the column-4 legs (4b.f and 4t.e) as side 1 and the column-6 legs (6b.f and 6t.e) as side 2. This matches the manual: 5V goes to one side, and pin 2 plus the pull-down go to the other side.
Pin 2 (teal wire) lands in column 6 at row i. The resistor's left lead is in column 6 at row c, on the same side of the button as pin 2, so it is the pull-down.

The orange wire runs from column 4 (row c) to the bottom plus rail and carries 5V to the button's other side. The 10k resistor goes from column 6 to column 9. The short black wire goes from column 9 (row b) to the bottom minus rail.
The hole numbers on the rails (bp.1, bp.3, bn.1, bn.7) are my estimate, counting rail holes from the left end of the board in groups of five.
The black wire from the Arduino ends on a GND pin in the power header. I used GND.2, the second of the two GND pins. The image shows the pin but the exact catalogue port is a guess.
The resistor value is given as 10000 ohms, from the manual's 10k ohm.

The Claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization before they can be used. This session is non-interactive, so they were not used. They can be authorized in the claude.ai connector settings. They were not needed for this task.
